post.caption: Miners reportedly used diamonds as game tokens. The story comes from Brazil in the 1720s. Until then, India was the world's main source of diamonds. Gold miners there found shiny stones in rivers and streams, and later accounts say some used them as markers in card games. Then someone who had been in India recognized them. In 1734, Portugal's crown marked off a Diamond District, and in 1739 the crown granted a private monopoly on the mining. Brazil became the world's top diamond producer, passing India. Then in the 1860s, diamonds turned up in South Africa.
